fact_checks: The verified-facts section has no structured evidence for the named ids, so the claim that every sibling has 'properties' is unconfirmed.
The current schema lists only two attributes for applicationinteraction, 'documentation' and a required 'pattern' enum; neither is a 'properties' attribute.

The layer skill overview mentions 'optional properties for external specifications (OpenAPI, orchestration definitions, event schemas)', which suggests some siblings carry such attributes. It does not say all of them do.

arguments_for: If every sibling really has 'properties', its absence here is an inconsistency that leaves modellers no place to attach saga or choreography spec references.
The layer intent names orchestration definitions as a use of optional properties, and interactions such as sagas are exactly where orchestration specs live.
A uniform attribute set across element types makes CLI validation and tooling simpler.
arguments_against: No verified fact shows that any sibling, let alone every sibling, has a 'properties' attribute, so the inconsistency itself is unproven.
Interaction already has a type-specific 'pattern' attribute, which suggests a deliberately tailored schema rather than an omission.

arguments_for: The skill overview calls properties 'optional' and scopes them to external specifications, so they may be intended only for types with OpenAPI or event schemas.
The required 'pattern' enum shows interaction was given its own attribute set on purpose.
ArchiMate 3.2 defines no generic properties bag per element type, so leaving it out may be intentional.
arguments_against: The overview names orchestration definitions explicitly, which maps naturally onto interactions like sagas, so excluding them looks accidental rather than designed.
Nothing in the definition or distinctions states that properties are intentionally withheld from interaction.

arguments_for: Whether interactions need an extension bag for orchestration specs is a product decision about how much metadata modellers attach.
The facts neither confirm nor refute sibling consistency, so the case rests on design preference rather than a provable error.
Adding an optional attribute is low-risk either way, so this is a matter of preference, not correctness.
arguments_against: If the siblings do uniformly have 'properties', this becomes a plain consistency defect, not a matter of preference.
If the omission is deliberate per the 'optional external spec' intent, this is simply works-as-designed.

arguments_for: A generic 'properties' bag may be a tooling or serialization convention rather than part of the ArchiMate element model the spec describes.
arguments_against: The claim is about the attribute schema of a spec element type, which is squarely within the spec's own content.
The layer overview itself discusses properties as part of the layer, so the topic is in scope.
